root_cause: ImageSetSampler (/mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/qt/widgets/preview_controls.py) uses ONE field, self._directory, for two different jobs. enumerate() writes and compares the composite cache key f"{directory}|{metadata_type}|{custom_regex or ''}"; adopt() writes the bare directory string. The two can never be equal, so the enumeration the worker thread hands the panel (LivePreviewPanel._on_source_payload -> sampler.adopt) is thrown away by the very next _refresh_source_selectors() -> sampler.enumerate(), which rescans the folder synchronously on the GUI thread. Proven, not read: a probe printed `after adopt, _directory = '/some/dir'` vs the key enumerate() computes `'/some/dir|cellvoyager|'`, cache hit? False; and a real panel load logged `enumerate_image_sets calls during one folder load: 2` with `sampler._directory = '/tmp/plate_.../plate1|cellvoyager|'`. In this test _panel_on() adopts 32768 synthetic sets, then load_image() triggers the rescan, which finds only the 60 files actually on disk -> 20 sets, so `before` is already 20 when it is read and `before == BIG_SETS` fails. The test's docstring anticipated exactly this detection ("a re-scan of this folder would find the 60 files that exist on disk instead of the 98304 sets the sampler was given, so a silent re-enumeration cannot hide") and it worked. Note the `calls == []` half PASSES: the rescan happens once per folder load, before the monkeypatch is installed, not per field change. Patching only the key/seed conflation in memory (no repo edit) made this test and the two below pass.
consequence: Opening a folder in the live preview enumerates it twice - once off-thread as designed, then again synchronously on the GUI thread - freezing the UI for a measured 152 ms on an 18432-file plate (~800 ms extrapolated to the documented 98304-file plate), which is the stall the async loader was written to remove; _on_source_payload's own docstring asserts this call "is a cache hit only because the worker's listing has already landed here", and that invariant is false.
suggested_fix: Stop conflating the cache key with the folder. Keep the real directory in a separate attribute (e.g. self._dir_path) set by both enumerate() and adopt(); have adopt() write the same composite key enumerate() compares against, so the worker's listing is a cache hit; and have the `seed` property derive from the real directory rather than from the cache-key string.

root_cause: Same ImageSetSampler defect, seen through its second face. `seed` computes sample_seed(self._directory, ...) and sample_seed() keys on Path(directory).name. After the spurious GUI-thread re-enumeration described above, self._directory is the cache key, so that name is 'plate1|cellvoyager|' rather than 'plate1'. load_source_payload() picked the field to open on using sample_seed(path.parent, ...) i.e. 'plate1'. Two different seeds, two different draws: the field the panel opened on is not in the sample the panel then lists, so ImageSetSampler.sample() pins it as an extra entry and _fov_box.count() is 21, not DEFAULT_MAX_SETS (20). Verified on a real panel: `pinned = ('plate1','A02','001')`, `loaded set in DRAW (unpinned)? False`, `note: showing a random sample of 20 of 192 image sets, plus the field you loaded`. Not stale: the +1 pin is a legitimate feature for a user-chosen file, but here nobody chose anything - the panel auto-loaded a field and then failed to draw the sample it had just used. Fails alone, and passes with the key/seed conflation probe-patched.
consequence: Every folder auto-loaded into the live preview opens on a field outside its own sample, so the panel shows 21 entries and announces "plus the field you loaded" when the user loaded nothing specific, and the reproducible seed it prints for hand-off is computed from a string containing '|cellvoyager|' so it does not match the seed anything else in the product uses.
suggested_fix: Same fix as the perf-guard entry: separate cache key from directory so the `seed` property hashes the real folder name, making the worker's draw and the panel's draw identical and removing the phantom pin.

root_cause: Identical root cause to the entry above - the seed the panel samples with is derived from the cache-key string, not the folder, so the auto-loaded field falls outside the panel's own draw. Failure is at line 276, `assert panel._fov_box.count() == DEFAULT_MAX_SETS` (21 != 20). Worth noting the assertion two lines earlier, `loaded.key in [s.key for s in panel._sampler.sample()]`, PASSES only because sample() adds the pin - it is masked by the same bug it should catch, and the count assertion is the one that exposes it. Fails alone; passes with the probe patch.
consequence: Same as above - the auto-loaded field is not one of the sampled sets, it survives in the list only as a pin, and the dropdown/table carries a 21st entry the user never asked for.
suggested_fix: One fix covers all three: give ImageSetSampler a real directory attribute distinct from its cache key, have adopt() write the composite key, and compute `seed` from the directory.

root_cause: The test dates to 2026-07-30/08-02 and encodes the pre-redesign Stop. Commit 5cb219f1 (2026-08-06, "stop: ask whether to wait or to kill, instead of asking once and hoping") deliberately changed AppScreen._on_stop (spacr/qt/screens/app_screen.py:2727) to (a) open the ask_how_to_quit modal first and (b) deliberately NOT disable the Stop button — its docstring states the reason verbatim: "NOT disabled. The test stubs neither the modal (hence the QMessageBox.exec headless guard firing at conftest.py:268) nor updates the button assertion. Verified empirically: with `monkeypatch.setattr(spacr.qt.shutdown, 'ask_how_to_quit', lambda *a, **k: GRACEFUL)` the whole scenario passes — buttonActionBusy is True, run button re-enables, _thread clears, console shows "Requesting stop" and "Stopped safely" and no "Failed — see traceback". The ONLY surviving contradiction is `assert not screen._btn_stop.isEnabled()`, which is the behaviour that was intentionally removed. Cooperative cancellation itself is not broken.
consequence: None — the product behaves as redesigned; this is a test that was not re-pointed when Stop gained its wait-or-kill prompt.

Keep the buttonActionBusy and console assertions as they are; they already pass. A companion case returning FORCE and one returning CANCEL would cover the two other branches.

root_cause: The test measures ONE displayed frame (`az.content_extent([frame])` on the first pixmap after reveal) and its inline comment states the premise: "`cell_diameter` draws its whole shape in every frame." That was true when the test was written (2026-08-03/04) and was deliberately made false by commit 97ba3e75 (2026-08-09, "The diameter animations drew a caliper over an object that never changed size"), which regenerated the four diameter GIFs so the object now scales with the animation instead of holding a fixed radius. Measured directly on the shipped asset: the 18 per-frame extents of the zoomed cell_diameter run 0.423, 0.432, 0.468, 0.532, 0.605, 0.668, 0.723, 0.759, 0.759, 0.750, 0.723, 0.682, 0.632, 0.568, 0.514, 0.468, 0.432, 0.423 — only 5 frames sit inside the 0.70-0.80 band, and frame 0 (the one the label shows) is the smallest at 0.4227, exactly the failure value. The zoom is correct and meets its documented contract, which is stated on the UNION across frames: spacr/qt/widgets/animation_zoom.py content_mask docstring — "The union — not one representative frame — is what has to be framed" — and ZoomedAnimation.measured_fill() for cell_diameter returns 0.759, inside the band. cell_diameter is not among the four animations that genuinely fall out of band.
consequence: None — the animation is correct and correctly zoomed; a pulsating diameter illustration necessarily has small frames, and the test asserts a per-frame invariant the design never promised.
suggested_fix: Measure the union rather than one frame: capture the frames the view holds (or use `az.zoomed_animation(path, HoverTooltip.ANIMATION_SIZE).measured_fill()`) and assert MIN_FILL <= that <= MAX_FILL. If the intent is to prove the widget is showing the zoomed frames rather than the raw GIF, a per-frame `extent <= MAX_FILL` plus a union-in-band assertion keeps that guarantee without pinning the smallest frame.

root_cause: Half-finished migration of the `classes` setting. Commit 30500970 ("classify: the Classes editor...") turned `classes` from a list of names into a dict of name -> {column, value} and routed the key to ClassEditorWidget (spacr/qt/screens/settings_model.py:4031), but the DEFAULT was never migrated: spacr/settings.py still does settings.setdefault('classes', ['nc','pc']). ClassEditorWidget.set_value (spacr/qt/widgets/class_editor.py:191-197) converts that legacy list into placeholder rules with column="?", so the panel collects {'nc': {'column': '?', 'value': None}, 'pc': {...}} where the module's declared default is ['nc','pc']. Same family as the classify_merged case: a new shape registered without its accompanying entries. Verified in a live panel: SettingsWidgets('classify')._defaults['classes'] == ['nc','pc'] while collect()['classes'] is the '?' dict. The test is a generic invariant (defaults vs collect), not retired behaviour -- once the classify default is expressed in the dict shape it passes unchanged, which is why I call it real rather than stale.
consequence: Opening Classify and pressing Run without touching the Classes editor ships class rules on a column literally named "?", so the run aborts with ClassDefinitionError: "class 'nc' is defined on column '?', which this table does not have" -- naming a column the user never typed. Additionally, because the collected value is now a Mapping, classify_classes.normalize_settings skips its legacy translation branch entirely (`if not isinstance(raw, Mapping)`), so the annotation_column / metadata-control translation the redesign promised can never fire on a GUI-collected settings dict.
suggested_fix: Migrate the product default, not the test: give classify (and deep_spacr) `classes` the dict shape ({} or a real rule dict) so the panel round-trips it, and stop emitting placeholder rules from collect() -- either drop rules whose column is the "?" placeholder, or keep the placeholder purely as display text.

root_cause: Test-harness scale mismatch, not product code. During the test the font-scale PREFERENCE reads 1.5 (probe: font_scale_pref=1.5) so scaled_px(WIDTH_MIN)=330 and scaled_px(WIDTH_MAX)=480, but the QApplication stylesheet was built by the session fixture tests/qt/conftest.py::qt_theme_applied calling theme.stylesheet() with NO font_scale argument, whose default is 1.0 (probe: SidebarItem font-size=13px, i.e. the unscaled sheet). So the bounds are measured at 150% while the button text is drawn at 100%: the 'Cellpose Model Comparison Workbench' row hints 302px, below the inflated 330px floor, and the column stays pinned at the floor. Why the preference is 1.5: tests/conftest.py::_isolated_qsettings_store (function-scoped autouse, added 2026-08-03) redirects QSettings to an EMPTY per-test directory, so get_font_scale() falls back to DEFAULT_FONT_SCALE=1.5 (raised from 1.0 on 2026-08-03, commit b530f70a). The fixture meant to prevent exactly this, tests/qt/conftest.py::_font_scale_starts_at_one (session-scoped, added 2026-08-04), writes 1.0 into the SESSION-level sandbox store before the per-test redirect happens, so its write is never in the store the test actually reads. consequence: None user-visible. The real app always applies the stylesheet with the preference's scale (spacr/qt/preferences.py:1950 passes font_scale=scale), so bounds and text are never measured at different scales outside the test fixture. Test-only artefact.
suggested_fix: Make the fixture honest: have qt_theme_applied build the sheet at the effective scale — qapp.setStyleSheet(stylesheet(font_scale=preferences.get_font_scale())) — or move the 1.0 pin into a function-scoped autouse fixture that runs AFTER _isolated_qsettings_store so it writes into the per-test store the test reads.

root_cause: The test is a blanket AST ban on any `.terminate()` call under spacr/qt (added 2026-08-03 in e0440529, the live-lock/core-dump fix that introduced bridge.drain_thread). It now reports two call sites — spacr/qt/screens/app_screen.py:2821 (AppScreen._force_stop) and spacr/qt/widgets/home.py:609 (home._terminate) — both of which were added DELIBERATELY and LATER: 35a05890 'Force quit, from Preferences and from the Home run banner' (2026-08-05) and 5cb219f1 'stop: ask whether to wait or to kill, instead of asking once and hoping' (2026-08-06). Those commit messages spell out the policy change: cooperative cancellation is still the default, force is a separate escalation reached only through ask_how_to_quit with a prompt that states what it costs, and request_cancel is always tried first. drain_thread is not a substitute for that path — it PARKS a wedged thread (bridge.py:796), i.e. the run keeps computing, which is precisely what the user pressing Force is trying to stop. So the product policy was deliberately redesigned and the guard test was never updated; the test predates the redesign by two and three days respectively, which is the textbook stale signature.
consequence: The blanket ban is stale, but there is a residual hazard worth a follow-up ticket rather than a triage failure: the Preferences force-quit path ends in os._exit so a corrupt heap cannot matter, whereas these two call sites terminate a QThread running Python and then keep the process ALIVE (home.py even does thread.wait(2000) afterwards). That is the exact scenario the ban was written for — a thread cancelled while holding the GIL can live-lock the app, one cancelled inside PySide can crash it later somewhere unrelated. So: clicking Force on the Home run banner or the module Stop dialog can leave spaCR wedged or crash it minutes later, on a path the user was warned about only in terms of half-written files.
suggested_fix: Narrow the guard instead of deleting it: allow terminate() only where it is immediately followed by os._exit, or maintain an explicit allowlist of the two warned force-quit call sites so a third one still trips the test. Separately, consider making the two surviving paths exit the process (as the Preferences path does) rather than terminating a Python thread and continuing.

root_cause: Leaked process-global logging state. Culprit isolated to tests/qt/test_cov_qt_app.py::test_launch_drains_the_ai_consoles_on_quit — running just that test then this one reproduces the failure; the whole test_qt_worker_teardown.py file on its own does not. That test calls app_mod.launch(['mask']), whose theme/preferences path runs logging_util.apply_level_policy(get_log_file_levels(), get_log_console_levels()) -> verbose_logger.apply_console_levels(DEFAULT_CONSOLE_LEVELS). That installs a mutable LevelSetFilter({WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL}) on the MODULE-LEVEL _ConsoleForwarder singleton, and nothing ever removes it. Probe output between the two tests: filters=[('LevelSetFilter', [30, 40, 50])], console_levels=[30, 40, 50]. This test logs at DEBUG (10), so every record is vetoed by the filter and the console target receives nothing; it fails on `assert seen, 'the console target received nothing at all'` -> `assert []`, never reaching the re-entrancy assertion it exists to make. Confirmed causally: pre-installing ONLY apply_console_levels({WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL}) via an autouse fixture, with no other test running, reproduces both console failures exactly. The file's _restore_console_target fixture saves and restores vl._console_ref but not the handler's filters or level.
consequence: None in the product — the console showing WARNING and above while verbose logging is on is intentional (spacr/qt/preferences.py:1995 comments that the per-level switches 'are the finer statement and have to be the one that lands last'). The failure is purely leaked test state.
suggested_fix: Extend _restore_console_target (or add a conftest autouse fixture) to save/restore verbose_logger._handler's filters and level alongside _console_ref; or have these two tests call verbose_logger.apply_console_levels({DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL}) explicitly so they do not depend on no LevelSetFilter having been installed. Fixing the leak at its source — restoring the console level policy after any test that calls launch() — closes both console failures.

root_cause: Identical single root cause to test_a_record_logged_while_writing_the_console_is_dropped: tests/qt/test_cov_qt_app.py::test_launch_drains_the_ai_consoles_on_quit calls app_mod.launch(['mask']), which via apply_level_policy installs a LevelSetFilter({WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL}) on verbose_logger's module-global _ConsoleForwarder that is never restored. root_cause: The `themed_home` fixture does `page.setStyleSheet(theme.stylesheet(theme_name))`, so `page.styleSheet()` IS the whole application sheet. The sweep then scans that whole sheet for dark-only hexes with a bare `#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}` regex that does not strip QSS comments. The single offender it finds, `#000000`, sits inside a comment in the QC-dashboard widget block: `the WINDOW colour -- #000000 on dark -- as a solid rectangle behind its` (added 2026-08-06 in 9cebd643, after the test was last touched on 2026-07-27). Verified programmatically: with `/* ... */` stripped, the light, cell and glass sheets contain ZERO dark-only hexes; with comments left in, each contains exactly one, the comment. Qt's QSS parser discards comments, so not one pixel is affected.
consequence: None. The flagged hex is inside a QSS comment that Qt never parses; it is a test-only artefact of a regex that does not skip comments combined with a fixture that hangs the entire app stylesheet on the widget being swept.
suggested_fix: In the test, strip `/\*.*?\*/` (DOTALL) from each `styleSheet()` before running `_HEX`, and skip the page's own sheet (the fixture set it to the full app sheet by construction, so it can never be an 'inline' colour).

root_cause: Identical to the [light] case: the only dark-only hex in the cell stylesheet is `#000000` inside the QC-dashboard QSS *comment* (`the WINDOW colour -- #000000 on dark -- ...`), reached because the fixture puts the whole app sheet on HomePage and `_HEX` does not skip comments. Stripping comments leaves the cell sheet with no dark-only hex at all.
consequence: None. Pure test artefact — a hex inside a QSS comment paints nothing.
suggested_fix: Strip QSS comments before the hex sweep, and exclude the page's own (app-wide) stylesheet from the per-widget scan.

root_cause: Two offenders, both false positives. (1) `HomePage inlines #000000` is the same QSS-comment artefact as [light]/[cell]. (2) `DangerButton inlines #ffffff` comes from `style_as_danger` in /mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/qt/shutdown.py:224, which emits `QPushButton#DangerButton:hover { background: {danger}; color: #ffffff; }`. The fill IS resolved from `active_palette()`; only the hover ink is the literal `#ffffff`, which happens to collide with the dark palette's `fg` and is absent from the glass palette (`fg` = #fafafa). Substituting the glass `fg` — which is what the test is asking for — would make contrast WORSE, not better: measured white-on-danger is 2.04:1 on glass vs 1.95:1 for #fafafa. So the flagged literal is not the 'wrong palette imported' defect this test exists to catch.
consequence: None for the assertion as written. Separately worth queueing (NOT what this test measures): the danger button's hover ink is only 2.04:1 on glass and 2.20:1 on cell because those themes use a pale red danger (#ff9a95 / #ff8f86) — neither #ffffff nor the theme `fg` is legible on it, so the hover state of Force-quit / Stop / Clear buttons is hard to read on those two themes.
suggested_fix: Strip QSS comments in the test, and either whitelist #ffffff as a constant role (it is already excused for `button_accent` and friends via CONSTANT_ROLES) or have `style_as_danger` pick its hover ink by contrast against the resolved danger fill rather than by palette lookup.

root_cause: In /mnt/firecuda2/codex/repo/spacr/spacr/qt/widgets/ai_toggle_label.py, `_refresh_style()` installs a new per-widget stylesheet with a bigger `font-size` AND bigger `padding` but never invalidates the label's geometry (no `updateGeometry()`/`adjustSize()`), so the label keeps the width it was granted at the old font size. `_apply_elision()` then measures the NEW font against the STALE `contentsRect()` — 42px width minus 2x15px padding = 12px of inner room — and elides. Reproduced outside pytest: a toggle built at 100% and then moved to 150% stays 42px wide and shows only the ellipsis for 'Live' (the 'AI' case elides all the way to the empty string, since QFontMetrics.elidedText returns '' when not even the ellipsis fits). Once the visible text shrinks, the label's size hint shrinks with it, so no parent layout ever gives the width back — verified by resizing the parent afterwards, which does not recover it. Built fresh at 150% the same widget is 63px wide and reads correctly, so this is strictly a live-update defect. The elision cap landed 2026-08-08 (1eedb705) to stop the toggle starving the settings column; the test predates it (b99ffc67, 2026-08-04). The deliberate change was capping the MINIMUM width — blanking the label on a zoom change is an unintended side effect, so the test's requirement still stands.
consequence: Raising the Zoom preference while a module screen is open shrinks that screen's 'Live' toggle to an ellipsis (and its 'AI' toggle to nothing at all), and it stays that way until spaCR is restarted, because MainWindow.refresh_theme rebuilds only the Home page (_rebuild_startup_page) and never the module screens.
suggested_fix: In `_refresh_style()`, after `setStyleSheet`, call `self.updateGeometry()` (and re-run `_apply_elision()` against the new hint); and make `_apply_elision()` never reduce the label below the ellipsis — if `elidedText` comes back empty, keep the previous text rather than blanking the widget.

root_cause: Same defect as the [Live] parametrisation, worse symptom. `AiToggleLabel._refresh_style()` grows font-size and padding without invalidating geometry; `_apply_elision()` then measures the 20px font against the 42px-wide widget's stale contentsRect (12px of inner room after the grown padding) and `QFontMetrics.elidedText` returns the EMPTY STRING because not even the ellipsis fits. Measured directly: at 100% the widget is QSize(42,26) showing 'AI'; after the zoom change it is still QSize(42,x) showing ''. The test's ink-row count therefore goes 9 -> 0. Constructed fresh at 150% it is 63px and shows 'AI', confirming the sizing itself is right and only the live update is broken.
consequence: Raising the Zoom preference while a module screen is open makes that screen's 'AI' toggle vanish entirely (blank, still clickable), and it never comes back without restarting spaCR, since MainWindow.refresh_theme rebuilds only the Home page.
suggested_fix: Call `self.updateGeometry()` after installing the new sheet in `_refresh_style()`, and guard `_apply_elision()` so an empty `elidedText` result is never applied.

root_cause: Passes alone (exit 0) and with its whole file (all 107 tests, exit 0). root_cause: The whole file passes alone (5/5, exit 0) and in the 4-file combination. It fails after tests/qt/test_field_fade.py — reproduced with `pytest tests/qt/test_field_fade.py tests/qt/test_widget_qss_is_complete.py`, giving exactly 'SettingsSearchPane has no rule in a freshly built stylesheet'.
